echa_euses_water_screening_case_family_v.displayName: ECHA EUSES water screening case family
summaryLines: This governed reference case family anchors one-compartment flowing-water screening interpretations against regulator-recognizable EUSES-style environmental exposure concepts.
It is used as a screening reference family for residence-time and bounded-clearance reasoning, not as a claim that Fate MCP implements EUSES directly.
applicabilityLines: Appropriate for reviewer-facing mapping of flowing-water screening concepts where bounded clearance and compartment residence time are material.
Not a substitute for full multimedia EUSES implementation or dossier-specific environmental exposure modelling.

sourceReferences.title: ECHA Guidance on Information Requirements and Chemical Safety Assessment
ECHA EUSES support page

reviewNotes: Use this case family to ground screening logic in regulator-recognizable water-compartment exposure concepts without overstating model equivalence.

epa_environmental_models_elapsed_time_ca.displayName: EPA elapsed-time environmental model case family
summaryLines: This governed reference case family anchors elapsed-time and post-release-decay reasoning against EPA environmental model evaluation principles.
It supports review of time-bucket semantics and bounded post-release decay behavior in deterministic screening outputs.
applicabilityLines: Appropriate when reviewers need to understand why elapsed physical time and post-release decay are preserved in the bucketed screening surface.
Not a claim of EPA model approval, calibration, or one-to-one equivalence with any EPA transport engine.

sourceReferences.title: EPA Guidance on the Development, Evaluation, and Application of Environmental Models

reviewNotes: Use this case family for reviewer-facing time semantics, not for hydrodynamic or site-specific transport claims.

epa_flow_through_water_screening_case_fa.displayName: EPA flow-through water screening case family
summaryLines: This governed reference case family anchors finite-duration flowing-water screening logic against EPA environmental model guidance for bounded transport and model-use transparency.
It is intended to ground release-to-concentration screening claims where advective loss acts as a flow-through clearance term.
applicabilityLines: Appropriate when reviewers need a regulator-recognizable case family for finite-duration flow-through water screening behavior.
Not a claim of calibration to a specific EPA fate engine or a substitute for routed hydrologic transport modelling.

sourceReferences.title: EPA Guidance on the Development, Evaluation, and Application of Environmental Models

reviewNotes: Use this case family to explain bounded flow-through screening logic without overstating site realism.

epa_post_release_decay_bucket_case_famil.displayName: EPA post-release decay bucket case family
summaryLines: This governed reference case family anchors post-release elapsed-time decay behavior in bucketed screening outputs against EPA environmental model evaluation principles.
It is intended for reviewer-facing discussion of why bucketed concentrations continue to decline after the declared release period ends.
applicabilityLines: Appropriate for time-bucket screening claims where elapsed time and post-release loss remain explicit in the model family.
Not a substitute for transient transport routing or full hydrodynamic time-series modeling.

sourceReferences.title: EPA Guidance on the Development, Evaluation, and Application of Environmental Models

reviewNotes: Use this case family when a reviewer needs to distinguish elapsed-time decay semantics from arbitrary bucket pagination.

epa_post_release_flushing_screening_case.displayName: EPA post-release flushing screening case family
summaryLines: This governed reference case family anchors post-release flushing and retained-mass decline against EPA environmental model evaluation principles for time-varying screening scenarios.
It is intended for reviewer-facing discussion of how retained mass should drain after emission stops when a residence-time clearance term remains active.
applicabilityLines: Appropriate when reviewers need a regulator-recognizable case family for post-release flushing or recovery interpretation in a deterministic flowing-water screening model.
Not a substitute for routed hydrodynamic transport, downstream travel-time modelling, or site-specific recovery observations.

sourceReferences.title: EPA Guidance on the Development, Evaluation, and Application of Environmental Models

reviewNotes: Use this case family to ground post-release retained-mass decline and flushing interpretation without overstating transport realism.

oecd_post_release_recovery_screening_cas.displayName: OECD post-release recovery screening case family
summaryLines: This governed reference case family anchors post-release recovery interpretation against OECD degradation-and-accumulation reporting concepts for deterministic screening models.

It is intended to support reviewer-facing discussion of retained mass decline after active emission stops, including the distinction between mass retained in the compartment and cumulative mass removed.
applicabilityLines: Appropriate when reviewers need an OECD-recognizable case family for post-release retained-mass decline, degraded mass, and flushed mass interpretation.
Not a substitute for OECD test execution, measured field recovery data, or full multimedia fate modelling.

sourceReferences.title: OECD Test Guidelines for Chemicals
OECD Harmonised Templates: Degradation and Accumulation

reviewNotes: Use this case family to explain post-release retained-versus-removed mass interpretation in a regulator-recognizable way without claiming OECD model equivalence.

echa_post_release_flushing_boundary_case.displayName: ECHA post-release flushing boundary case family
summaryLines: This governed reference case family anchors reviewer-facing interpretation of post-release recovery windows that sit near the one-turnover flushing boundary in a flowing-water screening model.
It is intended to explain why retained release-stop mass can remain boundary-sensitive even after active emission ends when residence-time turnover is close to one full flushing window.
applicabilityLines: Appropriate for post-release turnover-boundary and recovery-interpretation claims in the advective screening family.
Not a substitute for routed hydrodynamic recovery modelling, site observations, or full EUSES implementation.

sourceReferences.title: ECHA Guidance on Information Requirements and Chemical Safety Assessment
ECHA EUSES support page

reviewNotes: Use this case family when a reviewer needs an EU-recognizable explanation for why post-release retention and flushing can remain boundary-sensitive around a one-turnover recovery window.

epa_post_release_directionality_case_fam.displayName: EPA post-release recovery directionality case family
summaryLines: This governed reference case family anchors reviewer-facing interpretation of how retained release-stop mass should progress as the post-release recovery window moves from below the one-turnover flushing boundary to beyond it.
It is intended to ground directionality claims about retained-mass decline and bounded post-release flushing progression in a regulator-recognizable US environmental modelling posture.
applicabilityLines: Appropriate for post-release directionality claims that need explicit sub-boundary, boundary, and beyond-boundary recovery interpretation in the advective screening family.
Not a substitute for routed receiving-water recovery modelling, monitoring data, or calibrated hydrodynamic post-release analysis.

sourceReferences.title: EPA Guidance on the Development, Evaluation, and Application of Environmental Models

reviewNotes: Use this case family when a reviewer needs a regulator-recognizable explanation for why retained release-stop mass should cross below the one-turnover anchor as the recovery window extends.

epa_post_release_recovery_pace_case_fami.displayName: EPA post-release combined-loss recovery pace case family
summaryLines: This governed reference case family anchors reviewer-facing interpretation of how quickly retained release-stop mass should halve under the combined degradation-plus-clearance loss constant in a flowing-water screening model.
It is intended to explain why post-release recovery pace can cross the 50% retained-mass anchor before the one-turnover flushing boundary when degradation and advection both contribute to loss.
applicabilityLines: Appropriate for post-release recovery-pace claims that need explicit pre-half, boundary, and beyond-half retained-mass interpretation in the advective screening family.
Not a substitute for calibrated hydrodynamic recovery modelling, monitoring-derived depletion curves, or full receiving-water post-release analysis.

sourceReferences.title: EPA Guidance on the Development, Evaluation, and Application of Environmental Models

reviewNotes: Use this case family when a reviewer needs a regulator-recognizable explanation for why the combined-loss half-recovery pace can be materially earlier than the one-turnover flushing boundary.

oecd_post_release_half_recovery_directio.displayName: OECD post-release half-recovery directionality case family
summaryLines: This governed reference case family anchors reviewer-facing interpretation of how retained release-stop mass should progress from above the 50% combined-loss recovery anchor to materially below it as the post-release window extends under the same resolved loss constants.

It is intended to ground directionality claims about combined-loss post-release depletion pace in a regulator-recognizable international screening posture rather than leaving that interpretation implicit in raw decay math.
applicabilityLines: Appropriate for post-release half-recovery directionality claims that need explicit pre-half, boundary, beyond-half, and extended-beyond-half retained-mass interpretation in the advective screening family.
Not a substitute for calibrated receiving-water recovery monitoring, hydrodynamic routing models, or site-specific depletion-curve fitting.

sourceReferences.title: OECD Harmonised Templates: Degradation and Accumulation

reviewNotes: Use this case family when a reviewer needs an internationally recognizable explanation for why retained release-stop mass should not merely cross the 50% anchor, but continue moving materially below it as the post-release window extends.
